config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphGlobalMemo: Shared estimated workspace cap across concurrent snapshots, solvers, fallback and display jobs; default 512 MiB. Released on completion or cancellation. Separate from retained caches and work budgets; not a JVM heap cap. Reload affects new reservations, without revoking existing ones.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphCacheMemor: Global estimated retention target across AE networks; default 256 MiB, 0 disables retention. Estimates refresh after requests; excess least-recently-used captures are evicted every 20 ticks. Active snapshots live until their requests finish, so transient memory can exceed this target. No search work is charged.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphSnapshotMi: Cooperative allowance shared by all main-thread snapshots, default 2000 microseconds/tick. Idle chunks are capped at this value or 1000 microseconds, leaving 1 ms before the next tick. An indivisible operation may overrun. Reloadable.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphSliceSteps: Maximum cooperative steps per planning slice, default 4096. Yields at the first work or time bound. Controls fairness without increasing total request work. Requires server restart.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphSliceMicro: Cooperative time allowance per planning slice, default 2000 microseconds. An indivisible operation may overrun. Requires server restart.

Engine for new crafting jobs: LEGACY uses the original engine; GRAPH uses CGSE (Compiled Graph Solving Engine), supporting cyclic recipes. Restart required. AE2 calculation mode only affects LEGACY.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphIntelligen: GRAPH only; enabled by default. Use actual cycle returns to balance growth and downstream consumption, helping productive cycles increase batch sizes. Slower returns allow downstream work to proceed. Disable to use ordinary graph scheduling. Changes apply to running jobs.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphByteCostMo: GRAPH only. LEGACY (default) preserves the existing material, execution and dependency charges. COMPACT charges ceil(sum of initial required amounts / each key type's amount per byte) + 8 bytes per distinct used recipe task. Initial amounts include seeds and material awaiting external supply or refill, counted once. Intermediate products and repeated executions add no charge. This is an admission rule, not physical memory or peak inventory usage. Changes apply to newly calculated plans; existing previews retain their cost.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphDiscoverBy: Discover Byproduct Sources for Graph Crafting

GRAPH only; disabled by default. Index declared secondary outputs of registered patterns on this network and allow running a complete recipe to obtain its byproduct. All inputs and outputs belong to the same execution. Undeclared or random outputs are not inferred. May add alternatives, search cost and surplus primary outputs. Changes apply to new calculations.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphSeedPolicy: GRAPH only. PRESERVE retains or restores a seed that can restart the cycle after completion. ALLOW_CONSUME may consume seeds after their final use. Both protect seeds still needed for execution; expected returns are not treated as held materials.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphMaxExtraCa: Maximum Extra Catalyst Copies to Craft

Maximum additional catalyst copies to manufacture per cycle for parallel crafting. Uses existing stock first, then considers idle CPU co-processors and useful work. 0 disables extra production, but still allows required starting seeds. This is a ceiling, not a fixed quantity. Extra materials and recovered catalysts are included in the plan.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphPlannerNot: GRAPH only. Show planning progress after this delay from the start of the request. This controls the notice only and never stops a calculation.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphPlannerTim: GRAPH only. Wall-clock limit from the first actual computation, including subsequent waits. Reaching it stops the request. 0 disables the time limit; work and memory budgets still apply.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphPlannerThr: GRAPH only. Worker limit shared by all planning requests and parallel graph construction. More threads do not guarantee a faster request and increase CPU usage. Reload the world or restart the server after changing this.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphPlannerMax: GRAPH only. Maximum admitted planning requests, including waiting requests. New requests are rejected at the limit; retry later. Reload the world or restart the server after changing this.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphCompilerMa: Graph Compilation Work Limit (0 follows search budget)

GRAPH only. Independent graph compilation work allowance per request; does not consume search work. Default 0 uses the search limit; a positive value sets a separate base allowance with the same parallel budget multiplier. Compilation still shares request memory, timeout and cancellation limits. Applies to new calculations after config reload.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphCachePrepa: GRAPH only. Independent per-request allowance for preparing caches for future reuse; default 8192. 0 disables this optional preparation without clearing existing caches. All workers share this cap without a parallel multiplier or deductions from search/compilation. Exhaustion skips optional preparation without aborting solving; current-request deductions and validation still consume search work. Applies to new calculations after config reload.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphPlannerPar: Expand Graph Work Budget for Parallel Planning

GRAPH only; disabled by default. Uses the current planner worker limit to expand the configured cumulative work limit: 1 worker 1x, 2 workers 1.5x, 3 workers 1.75x, and 4 or more workers at most 2x. All branches share this single expanded cap; time and memory limits stay the same. Extra work can help difficult requests finish but can increase CPU use and waiting time. Applies to new calculations.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphFallback.c: GRAPH only; enabled by default. If the main solver cannot return a plan, expand ordinary recipes from the captured catalog once without cycle solving. Cycles and expansion boundaries become refill inputs. A fallback preview does not prove all routes infeasible. Uses independent fallback budgets, defaulting to 250 milliseconds, 131072 work units and 16 MiB of workspace. Cancellation, snapshot failures and unsupported pattern semantics do not trigger fallback. Applies to new calculations after config reload.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphFallbackTi: Only used when fast graph fallback is enabled. Independent wall-clock limit from fallback start, default 250 milliseconds. 0 disables this time limit; work and memory caps still apply. This time can be added after the main solver has stopped. Applies to new calculations after config reload.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphFallbackMa: Only used when fast graph fallback is enabled. Independent work allowance for ordinary recipe expansion, default 131072. No parallel multiplier, refund or borrowing from primary search. Increasing this value does not add cycle solving to fallback. Applies to new calculations after config reload.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphFallbackMe: Only used when fast graph fallback is enabled. Independent estimated workspace budget: 1–1024 MiB, default 16 MiB. Used on demand without preallocation. Does not change the JVM heap size. Applies to new calculations after config reload.
gtlcore.ae.graph.fallback_preview: Fallback preview (cycles skipped; missing inputs for this route)
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphPlannerMax: GRAPH only. Search and verification work limit per request. Graph compilation has a separate allowance of the same size by default, adjustable through the compilation work limit, without consuming search work; both share memory, timeout and cancellation limits. Regions, workers and continuations share each cumulative allowance. Parallel budget expansion applies its worker multiplier to this base limit. This does not limit recipe run counts or requested item amounts.
config.gtlcore.option.ae2GraphPlannerMem: Estimated Graph Planning Memory Limit per Request (MiB)

Estimated memory budget for each graph planning request: 16–1024 MiB, default 128 MiB. Used on demand, not preallocated; exceeding the budget stops that request. This is neither a JVM heap limit nor AE crafting CPU byte capacity. Concurrent requests have separate budgets, and actual process memory may be higher. Existing configured values are preserved.

config.gtlcore.option.bloom.comment: Client-local bloom settings. Changes from the config screen apply automatically; restart the client after manually editing the file.
config.gtlcore.option.bloomMode.comment: OFF disables integrated bloom and generated materials. AUTO uses local bloom without shaders and PBR with shaders. FORCE_LOCAL always selects local bloom. FORCE_PBR only uses PBR, with no local fallback when shaders are off. PBR requires a compatible shader. Forced local depth and reduced-resolution compatibility depends on the shader.
config.gtlcore.option.bloomStrength.comm: Local bloom intensity. Zero adds no halo. Adjusting this does not rebuild terrain caches.
config.gtlcore.option.bloomRadius.commen: Weights the blur scales; higher values favor broader halos.
config.gtlcore.option.bloomBuildBudgetMs: Soft budget shared by local emission geometry updates and uploads. Higher values reduce update latency but increase frame cost; individual model calls and uploads cannot be interrupted.
Generated PBR emission for textures tagged indicator.
config.gtlcore.option.screenEmission.com: Generated PBR emission for textures tagged screen.
config.gtlcore.option.coreEmission.comme: Generated PBR emission for textures tagged core.
config.gtlcore.option.defaultEmission.co: Generated PBR emission for emissive textures without a category. Ordinary textures do not become emissive.
config.gtlcore.option.generateSurfaceMat: Generate missing surface maps only for exact texture-hash profiles supplied by a resource pack. Authored surface channels take priority; unmatched textures are unchanged.
config.gtlcore.option.generateSurfaceNor: Generate normals only from explicitly supplied height masks in resource-pack profiles.
config.gtlcore.option.surfaceVariation.c: Roughness variation within generated surface materials; zero produces uniform roughness.
config.gtlcore.option.surfaceNormalStren: Strength of generated subtle normals. Only applies to textures with matching height masks.

config.gtlcore.option.minimumBlockMining: 0 disables the limit. Positive values cap normal player mining progress and prevent instant breaks. A value of 1 still requires a subsequent mining update. Slower blocks are not accelerated. Creative mode is unaffected.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiTagGrouping.com: Collapse matching items in JEI's ingredient list with a transparent expand indicator at the top right. Supports tags from all namespaces. Hover to expand and use normal recipe, usage, bookmark and drag actions. Client-local; changes apply after saving the config screen.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupHoverDelay: Time to hover over a group before expanding it. Scroll inside the popup to browse; press Escape to dismiss it.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupMetalBlack: Keep metal material forms such as ingots, nuggets, dusts, plates, rods and wires separate. Uses GT unification materials and Forge material-form tags, including alloys. Metal recycling components do not exclude finished containers or circuits. Tag and item blacklists still apply when disabled.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupTagBlackli: Full item tag IDs with * wildcards. An item matching any blacklisted tag always remains separate, even if it has other grouping tags. Ores, raw materials and processed ores are excluded by default.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupItemBlackl: Full item IDs with * wildcards, such as minecraft:oak_log or gtceu:*. These items always remain separate.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupPreferredT: First classify actual armor slots, stairs, slabs and walls, then try configured preferred, category, tool/weapon, supplementary and building tags. Automatic grouping recognizes known Minecraft/Forge item categories only; other mod categories must be explicitly configured. Functional tags such as destroyed-in-space or enchantable do not automatically form groups. Within a priority, choose more specific categories with fewer members. Blacklists always take priority.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupIgnoredTag: Broad tags that cannot define a group; supports * wildcards. Items may still group using other tags. Unlike the blacklist, this does not force items to stay separate. NBT variants retain their original data and can group by category or item; grouping pauses in JEI edit mode.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupCategoryTa: After preferred tags, use the first matching tag; supports * wildcards. Defaults group glass, chests, barrels, circuits and shulker boxes across colors, wood types, tiers and NBT variants. Configured categories also read matching block tags (such as minecraft:shulker_boxes in 1.20.1). Supports all namespaces. Blacklists always take priority.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupEquipmentT: After category tags, before same-item NBT grouping. Defaults group swords, pickaxes, axes, shovels, hoes and Forge tool subtypes across materials and NBT variants. Supports * wildcards; forge:tools/* creates separate groups for each tool type. Clear this list to disable this priority rule. Blacklists always take priority.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupSupplement: Defaults group the 16 glazed terracotta colors and match forge:armors/* categories. Armor also prioritizes its actual item slot, so mod armor missing Forge tags still groups separately as helmets, chestplates, leggings and boots instead of cross-slot functional groups. Supports * wildcards. Tag and item blacklists always take priority.
config.gtlcore.option.jeiGroupBuildingTa: Defaults group the 16 Ad Astra industrial lamp colors separately for regular and small lamps, plus stairs, slabs and walls. Building shapes are also classified from the block type, supporting AE2 blocks missing category tags. Supports * wildcards. Only specify category tags, not functional tags. Blacklists always take priority.
